protocol.invariant: Only the supplied goal-memory vector changes; live code, network weights, vision, task and reward are retained.
protocol.mirror_definition: Reflect arrival direction about the hit-to-true-center radial axis. Preserve 20cm shift and distance of predictive point to true goal; flip tangential component only.

equivalence_before_running.procedure: 90% paired t confidence interval inside [-5,+5], equivalent to 5%-level TOST.
equivalence_before_running.meaning: Exploratory coarse tolerance: half a goal per 90s episode; not absence of all arrival-direction use.

caveats: Center and mirror use privileged true goal center for diagnosis, not a realistic sensing improvement.
Mirror does not remove the radial arrival component and does not match wall proximity or all spatial relationships.
Evaluation-only changed goal messages, not retraining; input distribution effects remain possible.

validation.note: First-goal times and found-goal indicators match exactly across every goal-only variant within each model.

mirror_score_tolerance.interpretation: The 90% paired interval is entirely within ±5 score points.
mirror_score_tolerance.scope: Pre-run coarse score tolerance; unadjusted separate diagnostic. This does not establish identical mechanisms, directional information, or recurrent states.

statistics: Eight paired training-seed means are the replicates. Primary outcome: episode score; ten planned contrasts with paired 95% t intervals, paired t tests, and exact two-sided sign flips. Holm adjustments are supplied separately for the t and sign-flip p values within the ten score contrasts. Path efficiency and post-discovery goal rate are exploratory, each with the same separately corrected family. First-goal outcomes are validation/descriptive. Intervals themselves are unadjusted. Pickup-weighted geometry is descriptive and does not treat hits as independent statistical replicates.
limitations: Reflection preserves distance to the true goal center and shift length, but only reverses the tangential component of arrival direction.
A small reflection angle is a weak directional perturbation; a null effect does not rule out directional information use.
Equal distance to the goal center does not match wall proximity, grid-map responses, or routes from later spawn locations.
Center substitutions and the reflection use the hidden true goal location and are oracle diagnostics.
Current population code and frozen network weights stay intact; only the stored goal snapshot changes after pickup.
Closed-loop variants develop their own trajectories and later pickup snapshots, so geometry differences across variants can be consequences as well as causes of behavior.
